Title: MCP Search Tools Current State
Content: MemorySmith.App exposes POST /api/memories/search for Lucene.NET lexical ranking, POST /api/memories/search/semantic for semantic ranking, POST /api/memories/search/hybrid for Lucene.NET plus semantic RRF ranking, and /mcp for HTTP JSON-RPC tool access. Semantic ranking uses optional ONNX embeddings when configured and available, with local token/tag/title/reference/alias scoring as fallback. The HTTP MCP tools are memorysmith_search, memorysmith_semantic_search, memorysmith_hybrid_search, memorysmith_context_pack, memorysmith_get, memorysmith_page_search, memorysmith_page_get, memorysmith_unified_search, memorysmith_source_bundle, and memorysmith_find_by_source. memorysmith_search keeps its compatible tool name but returns lexical results rather than the old simple substring path. For larger KB workflows, prefer memorysmith_context_pack when an agent needs search results plus linked reference/conflict context in one response; it accepts query, ids, tags, status, limit, referenceDepth, maxContentChars, maxRecords, includeBacklinks, and format. Use format=json for structured parsing and the default markdown format for human-readable output. The tool reports warnings for missing roots, missing links, or omitted records after hitting maxRecords. .vscode/mcp.json points directly at http://localhost:5089/mcp. The /chat agent now uses ChatToolCatalog and an app-intercepted MCP-compatible read-only loop for memorysmith_unified_search, memorysmith_search, memorysmith_semantic_search, memorysmith_hybrid_search, memorysmith_context_pack, memorysmith_get, memorysmith_page_search, and memorysmith_page_get. It accepts model output shaped as toolCalls JSON or JSON-RPC tools/call, executes tools locally, and feeds results back into the same turn. ChatIntentInterceptor also handles clearly worded wiki intents before provider generation (for example, page get, context pack, and unified search). Source bundle and find_by_source remain HTTP MCP tools for external agents and are not chat-side model-requested tools. The implementation is covered by McpAndSemanticSearchTests, ChatToolCatalogAndInterceptTests, MemoryApplicationServiceTests, and PagesAndChatTests, which use copied Data/Memories fixtures so the source project wiki remains stable.
